an3.32:1.1: Ānanda (and others) ask a series of similar questions later in the Aṅguttara ([an10.6:1.2](), [an11.7:2.1](), [an11.8:2.1](), [an11.18:2.1]()). The question is whether it is possible to realize a state of meditation immersion that is based, not just on the temporary suspension of the five hindrances like the regular four absorptions, but on the permanent eradication of all defilements by the arahant. The commentaries identify this state as the “attainment of the fruition of arahantship”.
an3.32:2.1: “I-making” (_ahaṅkāra_) is the ongoing creation of the self or ego through thoughts that reinforce the self. | “Mine-making” (_mamaṅkāra_) is the same, but in regards to things felt to belong to the self, such as one’s body, property, or reputation. | “Underlying tendency to conceit” (_mānānusaya_) is the propensity or compulsion to form a self that remains even when there is no active ego-formation.
an3.32:5.1: This verse is at [snp5.4:6.1]() and is also quoted by the Buddha at [an4.41:6.1](). In both these cases, the verse evidently refers simply to the arahant, not specifically to a special state of meditation.
